_doc: Machine-readable statistical gate bans. Prose in ~/.gaia/knowledge/semantic-map/ has NO force over lanes; this file does. scripts/check_decision_gates.py enforces it. A result artifact may not carry a decision/verdict field if its producing script violates this file.

bans.reason: With-replacement resampling at small n duplicates rows (5.3/15 measured). The observed statistic barely moves; the permutation null inflates ~2.2x -> asymmetric bias -> the interval is structurally above 0 -> the gate is VACUOUS. Measured: fires 3/3 on pure unrelated random data, and the null-data CI is indistinguishable from the real-data CI.
bans.instead: Gate on permutation p (permutation preserves the row set). For anchor uncertainty use jackknife (leave-one-out), which creates no duplicates.
bans.allowlist_reason: archival r2 scripts, retained bit-unchanged as historical snapshot; superseded for decisions by lexical-r5-decision-record.json + run_intersection_r5_decision.py

bans.reason: Two CIs overlapping is not a test of their difference. Established in lighthouse PREREG r3.
bans.instead: CI of the difference itself (RD/RR Newcombe/Katz), or a permutation test.

bans.reason: embed_en is TRI-state: true=vector found / false=absent under this method / null=UNMEASURED. Truthiness collapses null into false, turning 'unmeasured' into 'absent'. Two independent auditors fell into this within one hour.
bans.allowlist_reason: these two ARE the detector for this antipattern (the pattern appears as a scanned-for string / fixture), not offenders
